newsitem.title: PERU: Peruvian priest is chess champion in hostage drama.
newsitem.headline: Peruvian priest is chess champion in hostage drama.

text.p: A Peruvian priest who turned down his chance of freedom to remain with hostages held by Marxist rebels in Lima has spent his time in captivity celebrating Masses and perfecting his chess game.

"We hostages maintain our unity and spirits, we pray together and sing ...I am unbeaten in chess after eight games with Japanese and Peruvian diplomats," Father Juan Julio Wicht wrote in a letter to his brother read out on Monday on local television.
Wicht was one of 83 VIP captives still held by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement guerrillas on Monday.
A Jesuit priest and university professor, Wicht was offered a chance to leave the Japanese ambassador's residence on Dec. 22 along with 225 hostages but chose to stay.
"I prefer to remain to help the hostages spiritually. I don't have any family," the priest was quoted as saying by former hostages.
Wicht, who offers regular Masses to hostages, asked his brother to send a book of hymns and fresh clothes.
"It is hot and we are sleeping on the floor," he wrote in the letter dated Dec. 26 and sent via the Red Cross. "The nights are long, without light, but God helps us."
